claim.pdf_says: FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 )  -- both FUNCTION and TEST-NUMVAL are underlined in the printed general format (verified at 300 dpi crop).
claim.why_it_matters: The transcription marks FUNCTION as a required word but silently drops the underline on TEST-NUMVAL on the same line, so the file is internally inconsistent about which tokens the standard prints as required words. Compare 15.92.2 on page 955, which correctly renders '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2)'. No syntax is made illegal here (the function name is required regardless), but the marking loss defeats any tooling that reads <u> to recover required words.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed; I tried to refute this and could not. (1) PDF side, measured not eyeballed: rendered page 956 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v956/spec_p956.png, 2550x3300). The 15.93.2 general-format line has its glyph ink in rows 977-1006 spanning x=271..1069. A horizontal rule exists on exactly one scanline, y=1021, and it is broken into TWO separate runs: x=273..471 (199 px) and x=498..777 (280 px), with a ~27 px gap between them and nothing at y=1020 or y=1022. The first run sits under 'FUNCTION', the second under 'TEST-NUMVAL', and the remaining ink 'x~790..1069' -- '( argument-1 )' -- carries no rule at all. The 2x LANCZOS crop (my_crop_fmt.png) shows the same thing visually: two distinct underlines, one per word, the second terminating at the final 'L' of NUMVAL before the open paren. There is no way to read this as a single rule, as a stray hyphen, or as scanner noise. (2) Markdown side: the repo file specs/ISO_COBOL.md (submodule d22c5e4a) line 38296 reads exactly '<u>FUNCTION</u> TEST-NUMVAL ( argument-1 )'. The claim quotes both sources verbatim; no misquote. (3) Not reflow/furniture: the token TEST-NUMVAL is present and correctly spelled -- the loss is the <u> markup on it, on the same line, so line wrapping, hyphenation and page-break furniture are all irrelevant. There is no 'Figure notes' annotation anywhere near line 38296 that records the marking, so the information is simply gone. (4) It does change notational meaning within the transcription's own metalanguage: ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.4 (md line 2631) says keywords 'are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats' and are required, while 5.2.5 (md line 2644) says optional words 'are shown in uppercase and not underlined' and 'may be written'. So as transcribed, 15.93.2 asserts TEST-NUMVAL is an OPTIONAL word -- i.e. that 'FUNCTION ( argument-1 )' would be legal. No human reader would be misled, which justifies the cosmetic severity, but the file states something the printed standard does not. (5) The internal-inconsistency argument holds: of the 20 intrinsic-function general-format lines in specs/ISO_COBOL.md beginning '<u>FUNCTION</u>', 18 underline the function-name; the cited comparator at line 38257 is '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u> ( argument-1 argument-2)' exactly as the claim states.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim is accurate as written; no correction needed to its substance. Two refinements for the ledger: (a) the defect is precisely a lost <u> wrapper on the function-name token, which under 5.2.4/5.2.5 reclassifies TEST-NUMVAL from keyword to optional word in the transcription's metalanguage -- so 'no syntax is made illegal' is right, but the file does make a false permissive assertion (that the name may be omitted), which is why it is worth fixing rather than waiving; (b) sibling sweep: this is one of exactly two exceptions among 20 '<u>FUNCTION</u> ...' general-format lines in specs/ISO_COBOL.md. The other is line 34556 on page 859, '<u>FUNCTION</u> CONVERT ( argument-1 source-format destination-format )', which is an unverified suspect for the identical defect class and should be rendered and checked in the same pass. Fix for this page: line 38296 becomes '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL</u> ( argument-1 )'.
